PullRequest.Title: test: gate Copilot restored-parent replay
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- temporarily disable the Copilot restored-parent replay scenario while OSS and product builds use different runtime versions
- document why one sequence-based fixture cannot replay both runtime request paths
- leave the existing OSS fixture unchanged

## Why PR CI did not catch this

GitHub Actions intentionally installs the public OSS runtime (`1.0.83-2`). The release product build rewrites only `@github/copilot` to `1.0.84-canary.67.g6496fad.unsigned` from the private feed. Canary 67 fixes optional custom-agent properties and introduces a successful child-model exchange, while the OSS fixture records the old `displayName: Required` failure. The PR suite therefore passed against the old request sequence and the product build failed against the new one.

## Validation

- live focused recording with canary 67 confirmed the underlying restored-parent behavior still passes
- full Copilot Agent Host E2E replay with canary 67: 176 passing, 22 pending
- `npm run hygiene`
- builds 471500, 471503, and 471513 showed the same stale-fixture failure on Windows, Linux, and macOS

The additional Windows file-edit failure in build 471503 was isolated: the same test passed on Windows in builds 471500 and 471513.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot Agent Host parity E2E suite registration and normal replay execution
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mocha registers the restored-parent scenario as skipped. Its callback never runs, so no per-test setup, session creation, model replay, restoration polling, or cleanup is on the suite's execution critical path; unrelated suite setup remains unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The skipped callback would create a temporary workspace and custom-agent file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one temporary directory plus directory/file writes per enabled Copilot parity scenario execution; after the diff, zero for this scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The scenario ran when provider was copilotcli with subagent support and performed the filesystem setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously synchronous filesystem setup preceded session creation; the diff removes it by unconditionally skipping the scenario.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/subagentSuite.ts:restored parent accepts a new turn after a custom subagent has no transcript
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The skipped callback would create/subscribe to an Agent Host session, dispatch two turns, unsubscribe/resubscribe, and wait for turn notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session with two turn sequences and bounded restoration polling per formerly enabled test execution; after the diff, zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The conditional test registration executed these IPC operations for supported Copilot configurations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations previously determined this test's runtime; the changed test.skip prevents the callback from executing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider/model requests are served through live recording or deterministic replay while driving the subagent and recovered-parent turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The test drove two parent turns, with runtime-dependent child-model request count; after the diff, no model boundary calls originate from this scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The enabled scenario consumed recorded/live model exchanges, including an additional child request in the product runtime described by the changed documentation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously on the test critical path; now absent because the scenario is pending.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one registration per parity target/provider suite; effective execution cardinality changes from one per supported Copilot configuration to zero. There is no collection-size or user-workload multiplier.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The scenario was one Mocha test within each enabled parity suite and its awaits serialized setup, restoration, and follow-up turn work. The diff does not add concurrency; it eliminates the scenario's execution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay fixtures and shared suite server leases remain unchanged. Because the callback is skipped, neither cold nor warm session/model state is exercised for this scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added line replaces conditional active test registration with unconditional test.skip, and Mocha does not execute skipped test callbacks or their per-test hooks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CI time saved depends on target/provider matrix and replay versus live recording, but the direction is strictly reduced work. Test coverage loss is correctness/process scope, not a performance regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff removes E2E filesystem, IPC, model, polling, and cleanup work rather than adding or amplifying it; it does not change shipped product code.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering and consumption of the known-issues documentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added Markdown is read by developers and repository tooling only; it is not imported or parsed by the Agent Host runtime.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed 17-line documentation addition with no user-data-dependent scaling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No runtime task, queue, or parallel operation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or invalidation behavior is touched.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed file is Markdown under the E2E test directory and contains no executable wiring.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; repository inspection shows this is documentation-only content.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the changed E2E registration through suite setup, session creation, filesystem setup, IPC, model replay, restoration polling, and cleanup. The only executable change unconditionally skips a previously conditionally enabled test, reducing CI work without changing product runtime behavior. No performance finding or regression-fix learning record is warranted.
